findings.summary: M18.263 made main green by having the spec press Shift+1 and Shift+0 until the result is right. The cause it diagnosed is a product race that a user meets the same way: the camera commands fit to the canvas size the editor last observed through useElementBox's ResizeObserver, so a fit pressed in the frame after a resize (here, focus mode) fits the old canvas. The author left it 'for cp42 to weigh'. It is real, small and reproducible, and it belongs to FR-EDT-002 (zoom to fit). The spec now proves only that the fit is right eventually, not that one press is.
findings.evidence: c1a8b65 body: 'Shift+1 fitted the 1632 x 1356 canvas from before focus mode, because the camera commands take the size the editor last observed (a ResizeObserver behind the DOM box the spec polls)'. progress.md M18.263: 'A user who presses a camera key within one observer delivery of a canvas resize gets the same stale fit; that is a product follow-up for cp42 to weigh, not this row.' packages/editor/src/canvas.tsx:262 `const box = useElementBox(ref)`. The spec at :71-78 wraps both key presses and the box assertion in expect(...).toPass(). The arithmetic in progress.md (z 0.8167 -> (-207.755, 177.551)) matches job 126697718487 exactly, so the cause is settled.
findings.failure_scenario: A person turns on focus mode or resizes the window and presses Shift+1 at once. The screen is fitted to the old size and sits off-centre or cropped, and a second press fixes it. No test catches a regression that makes the window wider, because the spec retries.

findings.summary: M18.259's check compares only the highest round the text names, plus whether any changes-requested line exists. A lost middle round passes. The acceptance says the gate fails a commit whose body 'names more review rounds than the digest lines for its row'. A body 'r1 changes-requested, r2 changes-requested, r3 pass' over digest lines r1 changes-requested and r3 pass names three rounds and holds two, and the check accepts it. That is the exact ledger gap cp38 F4, cp40 F1 and cp41 F1 were about, one round deeper.
findings.evidence: missingRounds (review-content.mjs:238-248): `held = max(round numbers)`, a miss only when `named.max > held` or a changes-requested round is named and none is held. Probe: namedRounds('...Reviewed: r1 changes-requested (a), r2 changes-requested (b), r3 pass.', 'M18.9') = {max:3, changesRequested:true}; missingRounds(that, [{round:'r1',verdict:'changes-requested'},{round:'r3',verdict:'pass'}]) returned []. The replay store (review.mjs) makes a reset less likely, but the check is the gate of last resort.

The connector, catalog and harness rows fit together: M18.260 reports what M18.239 drops, M18.261 closes M18.216's minors, and M18.259 closes the round-count reset with a store plus a message check. M18.218 completes ADR-0211's summary line on both surfaces and returns the eval prompt to the full catalog, and the recordings match 2c236ec exactly. Two things pull against each other.
